cards.title: Introduction to Vue Styling
cards.content:
Vue.js provides a robust, flexible approach to component-scoped styling out of the box using Single File Components (SFCs).

You can write standard CSS, use the scoped attribute for encapsulation, or leverage CSS preprocessors like Sass and Less.

cards.title: How Scoped CSS Works
cards.content:
When the scoped attribute is present on a <style> tag, its CSS will apply only to elements of the current component.

<style scoped>
.example {
  color: red;
}
</style>

Vue achieves this by using PostCSS to inject a unique data attribute (e.g., data-v-f3f3eg9) to DOM nodes and selectors.

options.text: It applies global styles to the entire application.
It restricts CSS rules to the current component only using unique attributes.
It compiles CSS into inline styles directly on the HTML elements.

cards.title: CSS Modules in Vue
cards.content:
A <style module> tag is compiled as CSS Modules and exposes the resulting CSS classes to the component as an object called $style.

<template>
  <p :class="$style.red">This is red</p>
</template>

<style module>
.red { color: red; }
</style>

cards.title: V-Bind in CSS
cards.content:
Vue 3 SFC style tags support linking CSS values to reactive component state using the v-bind() CSS function.

<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
const themeColor = ref('red')
</script>

<style scoped>
div {
  color: v-bind(themeColor);
}
</style>

pairs.right: Appends data attributes to limit CSS to the current component
Exposes CSS classes as an object named $style
Connects reactive script state directly to CSS property values
Applied across the whole app without encapsulation

cards.title: Order the steps to use Sass in a Vue SFC

items.text: Install sass dependency via npm (npm install -D sass)
Add lang="scss" or lang="sass" to the style tag
Write SCSS/Sass syntax inside the style block
Build and run the project to compile styles

cards.title: Deep Selectors
cards.content:
Sometimes you want a scoped style to 'bleed' into child components. You can use the :deep() pseudo-class:

<style scoped>
.a :deep(.b) {
  /* styles child elements */
}
</style>

cards.title: Styling Summary
cards.content:
You've learned the primary styling mechanisms in Vue.js:

  • Scoped CSS for local encapsulation
  • CSS Modules for programmatic class naming
  • v-bind() in CSS for dynamic reactive styles
  • :deep() for targeting child components
